I've left out `ReceiveMessageFrom` as the `SocketFlags` does return data from the operation:
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/69de57bcf2677238bbfb88e601bc38b89dc11dc0/src/libraries/System.Net.Sockets/src/System/Net/Sockets/SocketAsyncContext.Unix.cs#L1810

> My recommendation would be to change the existing `SocketHelperTask` and `SocketHelperSpanSync` to elide `SocketFlags` in their calls to `Socket`

Done.



> @geoffkizer do you think it's a useful overload regardless? The approved proposal is also questioning them: [#43934 (comment)](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/43934#issuecomment-900535135)

I'll add that also in the sync overloads, there's an overload for `ReceiveFrom` that elides the flags, which are **not** passed by ref, but there isn't one for `ReceiveMessageFrom` which passes the flags by ref.

> My recommendation would be to change the existing SocketHelperTask and SocketHelperSpanSync to elide SocketFlags in their calls to Socket. We aren't really testing the effect of SocketFlags in those tests anyways. @geoffkizer do you agree?

Just to be clear -- the idea here is that we cover these new overloads by making some of the existing test variations use them, but leave some using the old overloads so we continue to have coverage for those as well?

That seems reasonable to me. 

Let's make sure to add comments that explain this, otherwise it will be far from obvious and we'll look at the code in the future and say "why are we using these overloads here but those overloads there??"

> I'll add that also in the sync overloads, there's an overload for ReceiveFrom that elides the flags, which are not passed by ref, but there isn't one for ReceiveMessageFrom which passes the flags by ref.

This is a strong argument for not eliding the flags on ReceiveMessageFrom.

comments:

> This argument is rarely used.

Agreed, this will simplify call sites and improve readability. I think we should go for an API proposal. Is it just an overlook that these overloads were missing from the original proposal for `SendAsync`/`ReceiveAsync`, or was there a practical reason?
I don't think there was a practical reason, aside from just keeping the API surface minimal.
This seems reasonable to me, especially considering we have already approved UDP APIs with these overloads.

Triage: Let's add them from consistency reasons.
Should be simple once the API go through API approval.
@antonfirsov Do you want to put together the actual API proposal?
@geoffkizer edited the opening post, hope all overloads are included.

The new overloads for SendToAsync, ReceiveFromAsync, and ReceiveMessageFromAsync in https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/33418 aren't included above. I think we should include them for completeness, even though they have technically been approved already.
Yeah. Also, we should make sure to merge this API back into https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/33418 once approved.
Ok, will add tomorrow, thanks for checking!
Done, PTAL
Looks good
According to #43901, we should move the proposed methods to the `Socket` class. Will update the proposal later.

Is it possible to use default arguments (`socketFlags = SocketFlags.None`) here?
This shouldn't be a breaking change, as the overload with `socketFlags` is already there.

For most overloads this could be used. Some of them have the `socketFlags` in a position where this wouldn't work, so the new extra overloads is needed. But where possible I prefer the default argument.
My understanding is that isn't possible to do, though I'm not sure why. @terrajobst would know.
I do wonder if we should wait a bit here until we figure out scatter/gather APIs. If we have new and improved scatter/gather APIs, we should only add overloads for those.

Same for 8th method

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/24971b0a8b0c26ed9c1080c10d2f3c2f3f9f1ffd/src/libraries/System.Net.Sockets/src/System/Net/Sockets/Socket.Tasks.cs#L442

As long as it's there in the reference assembly declarations, it should work fine:

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/24971b0a8b0c26ed9c1080c10d2f3c2f3f9f1ffd/src/libraries/System.Net.Sockets/ref/System.Net.Sockets.cs#L386

However we should have probably assigned the defaults in the implementation declarations too for clarity and consistency.
